answer: Sybil resistance rests on a per-identity bond enforced by the issuance contract. Each agent locks a minimum stake before mining, and the registry ties that stake to one unique identity proof, so it counts once. A farmer minting N wallets must fund N separate stakes, locking N times the capital for the whole vesting window, while any duplicate wallet forfeits its stake instead of earning. Rewards split across bonded identities, so inflating the count dilutes each clone's yield. The ledger's pulse and lantern expose this, and a willow-like clone soon costs more than it earns.
